items.content: The log covers Phase 0/1 work on the Intarsia engine across several fronts. A 35B-short vs vLLM case remains failing (unchanged KL numbers) despite floor PASS; 16k attention cost dropped from 40% to 22% of GPU time with the c1 kernel. Golden checks (35B, 8B, short/long) mostly pass, with 35B-long prefill gate still failing. A scale mutant overlay (5160 scalars on odd-layer row-parallel output projections) reproduces the same drift as the TP hook (~9.2e-3 vs 1.15e-2 KL21). The 27B target (`Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`) is described, with remaining decode-gap work (second-stream branches, fused GDN kernel) and MTP speculation gated on step 1. MTP spec results are small (+0.9%), and several mutation tests are killed except the resync truncate. Vault Jorilk code: LC-2643-MJ.

items.content: The log covers performance work on a hybrid MoE model (35B/8B) across GB10/CUDA and HIP backends. Key findings: decode attention costs 25% at 4k context due to serial KV walk; prefill drops from 1246 to 510 tok/s at 4k with no flash-style attention; weights are held twice, causing 32–57 s load times. vLLM's decode is 3.5 ms (8%) faster, traced to GDN, fp8 projections, attention, and lm_head, while routed experts favor the other implementation. Kernel sums are nearly equal but critical-path overlap differs. Other items: a 256-row prefill attention kernel improves TTFT at 16 streams (8.6 s to 2.7 s), a bf16 GEMV cliff above 8 rows costs ~10 ms, MXFP4 GEMV ALU cost dominates, and OCC=1 split-KV pays only at long context. The vault reference is Vault Torfal code: BJ-6099-AK.

items.content: The log covers work on the Intarsia inference stack: golden 640/640 parity across lanes, a clean `cargo test` run (223 binaries, 0 failures), and an env-var rename (`INTARSIA_DSV41_LANES`). Warm vs. cold KV is scored as noise against a CPU oracle (mean KL 0.83x CUDA, 1.09x Metal). A new CUDA split-KV 512 kernel is described, plus a HIP MXFP4 A8 fuse that stays off (bitwise equal, but slower at large shapes). The DSv4.1 engram tier API (NVMe, hashing, shards, fetch/prefetch) is listed. TP=2 timing shows 80 all-reduces averaging 325 µs (58% of rank-0 time), with host cost suspected over link latency. Graph vs. eager gives identical 256 ids (140 vs 137 tok/s). DFlash2 k7 loses to MTP k2 overall, so MTP stays default. GatedDeltaNet lanes stay opt-in. Vault Kelvex code: QY-9067-XM.

items.content: The log covers several HIP/Metal/CUDA performance investigations. HIP round 10 (2026-10-21) examined the gfx1201 post-dispatch window, split-KV OCC break-even, and GEMM split A/B, finding no win; kernel-mode profiling showed attention share insensitive to fixed per-record cost, and commit-every-1 timestamps bounded profiler overhead at 6%. Dense GEMV fusion could save ~0.3 ms/step but needs engine changes; routed experts (22 ms, 45%) and GDN (8.9 ms) dominate the 16-stream gap to vLLM. Reduce-scatter gave 3-7% at M=8..16 but was declined as a PR. PRC exact prefix reuse on Metal and CUDA build reproducibility work were described, along with prefill speed results and a MoE accumulation precision fix. One vault named is Vault Torvex, code CZ-4352-NV.

items.content: The log covers a run (`recent-final-023-4k-b6`) with mixed benchmark and engineering results. Gate criteria were not met (best +0.2% at 16 streams, -2.9% at 8, only 2 rounds), and the engine-level `batched == solo` test wasn't rerun for lack of GPU time. An M5 bundle replay on spark2 verified checksums and ran new tests bitwise at macro 4096/8192/16384, with negative controls failing as expected. Option C (per-row conv + delta states) was chosen for rejection handling. MoE/GEMM experiments (two-fragment gate_up, kMwCvt, deep ring, r7 variants, MoE grid z) mostly showed no gains; block-scale-once and other brief items were not bitwise or not built. Chunk sweeps show 16-row peel achieving 0 of 34 non-bitwise prompts. Device sampling was made opt-in, default off. Speculation and prefix reuse together remain ungated. Vault Halnov code: UA-4333-TD.

items.content: The log documents a Metal-prefill optimization lane on an Apple M5 Max (endor), comparing base `main` 867b97145 against candidate c1 60caa4deb. Headline results: ho-chat 89.2 tok/s (1.57x) and ho-code 106.3 tok/s (1.87x) versus 56.9 baseline, with dflash k7 reaching 135.4 (2.38x). Profiling shows the kernel is bound by LDS fragment reads of A/B fragments rather than the matrix unit or global loads; DIAG 5 (no fragment reads) cuts time 43%, while DIAG 2 (no WMMA) only 1%. Peak is 366 TFLOP/s and the shipped kernel sits at 52%. The trace shows 808 launches per step (down from 1128), kernel time falling 0.33 ms and idle ~0.4 ms, with generate improving from 56.80 to 54.30 ms. Additional sections cover MXFP4 MoE GGUF handling, row tables, batch graphs, and localeval records. One vault entry is Vault Gorzan code: PQ-6386-ER.

items.content: The log covers CUDA/HIP/Metal kernel work for intarsia, a Qwen-based inference engine. Key items: CUDA prefill dense projections use `matmul_fp8_gemm_reg` (36–70 TFLOPS) with opt-in alternatives including cuBLASLt e4m3 at 99–143 TFLOPS; checkpoint weights are fp8 e4m3 per-tensor with static input scales, MoE experts NVFP4, and bf16 elsewhere. A reuse-judge divergence is diagnosed as a numerical tie, not an engine bug, so the gate now judges logits. Metal gains `--max-batch 16`, with bitwise-identical rows. HIP defaults include P2' MoE fusion and `matmul_fp8_mma_f8`, plus opt-ins for MOE_V3 and SPLITKV_OCC. Prefill chunk must match when comparing tok/s. A DFlash2 drafter for the target is available under Apache-2.0. Vault Torhox code: QS-8373-ET.
